CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain and swelling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports stepping off a curb yesterday during a walk with his wife and landing on his left ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing a pop but describes the ankle as feeling extended and stretched. Pain is located on the outside of the ankle and has been present since the incident. He was able to walk back to the house but with significant pain. He rates his current pain as 8/10 without medication and approximately 7/10 with ibuprofen. He has been managing the injury with ibuprofen, elevation, icing, and weight-bearing restrictions.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No substantial prior injuries to left ankle.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient takes regular walks with his wife. Works from home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable with slight elevation. Left ankle examination reveals ecchymosis over the lateral malleolus with swelling and edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No laxity appreciated in the joint. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular examination of left foot shows brisk capillary refill (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses, and intact motor and sensory function bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol with elevation and compression. Air cast prescribed for stabilization. Crutches prescribed; patient to remain off leg but start walking as tolerated. Continue NSAIDs for pain and swelling reduction. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient to return sooner if significant pain or concerns develop.
